events.note: Built by the Forest Service; NPS inventory form credits USFS employee Oscar Banner. Seattle Times and firelookout.com also give 1932. NHLR gives 1933 (see resolved_conflicts)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1933. The NPS inventory form, Seattle Times and firelookout.com give 1932. The story uses 1932 and reports the NHLR date.

Distances differ: NHLR gives 23 miles from the nearest road (or 13 miles up Ross Lake plus 7 miles of trail); Seattle Times gives a 4.7-mile trail from Ross Lake; Wikipedia gives 15 miles from the nearest road. The story reports all three.
NHLR gives 5,982 ft (1,823 m) and Seattle Times gives 6,102 ft. The record's 1823.3 m matches NHLR and is kept.
The NPS inventory form gives the cabin as 14 ft 6 in square; NHLR and the Seattle Times give 14 x 14 ft. The record and story use 14 x 14 ft, per NHLR.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflicts: NHLR says 1933; NPS inventory form, Seattle Times and firelookout.com say 1932 (the NRHP record also keys 1932 as its significant year). Distance to the site conflicts across three sources. Elevation differs (NHLR 5,982 ft; Seattle Times 6,102 ft; the NPS form's elevation is garbled in the OCR). The Seattle Times profile is undated in the copy read, so the staffing as_of is undated. No source states whether the cabin is open to visitors, so access level 'restricted' is an inference from its active NPS-staffed status. The brief's agency 'U.S. Dept. of the Interior' is the department; the operating bureau is the National Park Service. No specific fire the lookout helped fight appears in the sources read, so no fire events were added. Not checked: whether the NRHP nomination (NRIS 88003451) gives a different build year; the nomination PDF was not retrieved. Owner-supplied photo credit on the NHLR page ('courtesy of Jim Henterly') has no image URL, so no photo entry was added.
